title.narrative: RECRUITMENT, TRAINING AND DEPLOYMENT OF PRE-ELECTION LONG-TERM OBSERVERS (LTO)

description.narrative: CODEO deployed 100 observers for the pre-election observation of the electoral environment. Out of the 100, thirty (30) observers were trained and deployed through the financial support from the Netherlands Embassy, and the remaining 70 were deployed with the financial support of the CEPPS/NDI. Observers went through interview processes and were trained for two days in two clusters. The long-term observation was for a period of 10 weeks before the election day. The observers monitored constituency-level pre-election activities of key election stakeholders, including the Electoral Commission (EC), the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE), the National Peace Council (NPC), security agencies, political parties, traditional and religious leaders, civil society/community-based organizations (CSOs/CBOs), and the media. They also looked out for incidents such as intimidation and harassment of political opponents and citizens, violence, vote buying, destruction and removal of party paraphernalia, use of abusive and inflammatory language or hate speech at party rallies, human right abuses, destruction of public property, violation of election procedures, chiefs engaging in partisan politics, abuse of incumbency, among other things.

activity-date.narrative:
Recruitment and Deployment From the 19th to the 26th of September 2024, the CODEO Secretariat began its preparations towards long-term observation by conducting a series of interviews for applicants who expressed interest in being long-term observers. Out of the 30 observers that were funded by the Netherlands. Out of the 30 youth observers, 11 were females, 19 were males, and also there was one Person with Disability. A two-cluster training was scheduled for Kumasi and Koforidua on the 28th and 29th September, where the former combined observers from the Northern, Upper East, Upper West, Bono, Bono East, Ashanti, Western North, Ahafo, North East, and Savannah regions (Northern Zone) and the latter combining observers from Greater Accra, Volta, Oti, Western, Central and Eastern regions. Aside from the overview of CODEO and its observation activities, participants were taken through the following topics during the training: • Election Observation: Underlying Principles (International & Domestic Electoral Laws) • The 2024 Elections in Perspective and CODEO’s Observation Project • Observing the Pre-Election Environment (Long-Term Observation) • Serving as a CODEO Observer: Roles, Dos and Don’ts and Personal Security of the Observer • Data Protection (CyberSim Security) • Safeguarding, Anti-Corruption, and Sexual Exploitation Policy of CODEO • Observing the Pre-Election Environment using the CODEO LTO Observer Checklist and Incident Forms • Reporting through the CODEO Observation App
Two (2) simulation exercises were also held for participants during the training. Observers were deployed on 1st October 2024 to begin their long-term observation of their various constituencies .

Reporting of Pre-election Long-Term Observation Observers were required to submit a weekly report based on their observations by completing the questions on their checklist and promptly reporting any incidents as they occur. Two reports (1st November 2024 and 18th November, 2024 ) were published before the general elections .

title.narrative: CODEO calls on election stakeholders to intensify civic and voter education, stop vote-buying abuse of incumbency, and maintain peaceful and issue- based campaigns ahead of the December 7 elections

description.narrative: CODEO is pleased to share this second report from its observation of the pre-election environment ahead of Ghana's December 7, 2024, presidential and parliamentary elections. This report covers October 26–November 8, 2024, which is part of CODEO’s comprehensive observation of the upcoming elections. The findings presented here are based on weekly observation reports filed by 97 CODEO Long-Term Observers (LTOs) from 97 constituencies across all regions of the country. A total of 193 weekly reports filed by these observers during the reporting period were analyzed for this report. Summary of Findings • Improvement in voter education efforts by the Electoral Commission of Ghana. • Dominance of the political campaign scene by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC). • Marked differences in the campaign issues by the NPP and the NDC. • A generally peaceful political climate in the observed constituencies. • Instances of incumbency abuse, including using state resources such as public vehicles and government-owned equipment for campaign purposes.

title.narrative: CODEO identifies limited voter education in pre-election period - calls on stakeholders to increase engagement across constituencies: pre-election observation statement from October 1 - 25, 2024

description.narrative: The Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO), as part of its comprehensive observation of the December 7, 2024 presidential and parliamentary elections of Ghana, deployed 97 Long-Term Observers (LTOs) across the country from October 1, 2024. The observers were deployed to 97 purposively selected constituencies, which include a mix of constituencies considered stronghold or swing/competitive (of the two major political parties), hotspot constituencies, as well as some constituencies along border communities in the country. Since their deployment, CODEO’s observers have been monitoring the general electoral and political environment, including the activities of key election stakeholders such as the Electoral Commission (EC), the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE), political parties, security agencies, Civil Society/Community-based Organizations (CSOs/CBOs), and religious and traditional leaders. CODEO is pleased to share its first report from its observations of the pre-election environment covering the period, October 1 to October 25, 2024. This report is based on weekly observation reports submitted by CODEO’s LTOs. The findings presented in this statement are based on a total of 388 reports filed by our LTOs from the 97 constituencies for the period observed.

title.narrative: CODEO Deploys 100 Long-term Observers (LTOs) Ahead of the 2024 Presidential and Parliamentary Elections

description.narrative: 100 per-election observers were trained, 27 of these observers were funded by the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs. These 27 observers were youth with no prior experience in election observation—the training equipped them with the general election observation and the role of observers in promoting electoral integrity. They observed the pre-election for a period of two months and produced reports on the pre-electoral environment of Ghana's 2024 elections.

title.narrative: CODEO Deploys 100 Long-term Observers (LTOs) Ahead of the 2024 Presidential and Parliamentary Elections

description.narrative: CDD-Ghana/CODEO recruited 100 pre-election observers out of which 27 were funded by the Netherlands Embassy in Ghana.

Youth participation in election observation in Ghana is low. Over the years, the youth are used by political parties to mostly cause chaos at the polling stations and during the pre-election and post election phases. To effectively channel the energy into positively promote electoral integrity in Ghana, we trained them to observe the pre-election environment.
